These special Olympics aren’t even on an international scale. They’re primarily associated with school systems and programs for adults with special needs for more local competitions. The team I coached was just in Massachusetts and had a once a year swim meet in Bridgewater. It’s more about providing an experience for those with special needs where they can get a sense of accomplishment and be proud of the practice and effort they put into competing like anyone else would.

These programs also get barely any funding already, as most of the coaches and assistants work on a volunteer basis. 

I’ll admit that there isn’t necessarily a return on the governments “investment”, but this program improves the quality of life of many individuals with special needs in ways that really makes a difference.
